items.title: Obsidian ships official agent connectors: skills that let Hermes, Claude, ChatGPT and others read and write a local vault
items.summary: Obsidian now publishes official skill packages (Obsidian Flavored Markdown, Bases, JSON Canvas, the Obsidian CLI, Headless Sync and Publish) so any agent can use a vault as a shared, user-owned knowledge base. Nous added it to the Hermes Agent plugin marketplace as a verified, instructions-only package, so Hermes users can point their agent at their notes today.

doubt.pushback: Repliers point out the 'connector' is a set of skills, not an MCP server, needs the desktop app running or Headless Sync, and that agents could already work on an Obsidian folder.

reception.summary: Mostly enthusiastic about user-owned shared context across agents; skeptics say it repackages what a local folder plus skills already did, and one user benchmarking it says CLI lookups and edits cost more at equal or slower speed.

items.title: Hugging Face trains a four-agent swarm on one shared Qwen3-0.6B policy: team success 6.6% to 82.3% with 37% fewer tokens
items.summary: Part 1 of a Hugging Face series reproduces the s3 information-sharing task with TRL async GRPO: four agents with private inputs learn to message each other under a token-penalized team reward. The post gives the training loop, reward and a roughly $20 to $50 reproduction path, so builders can test whether multi-agent setups actually cooperate rather than just spend more compute.

items.title: JetBrains releases Mellum2.1 Instruct, a 12B-A2.5B open coding model for sub-agents and tool loops, with an MTP head
items.summary: Mellum2.1 Instruct is the non-reasoning sibling of Mellum2.1 Thinking (same MoE architecture and RL post-training), uses about half the tokens of Thinking on agentic coding tasks, and ships with a multi-token-prediction head for up to 1.8x faster generation. GGUF builds run through llama.cpp; one roster builder reports 25 to 30 tokens/s on an M3 Pro laptop.

items.title: Texas A&M measures GPU memory traffic over NVLink C2C on DGX Spark (GB10) with CUPTI L2 counters, within 0.005%
items.summary: On GB10 every GPU L2 miss crosses NVLink C2C to CPU-attached LPDDR5X, yet DCGM, NVML, nvidia-smi and the Linux C2C PMU expose no byte counts. The paper samples five L2 sector counters every 10 ms via CUPTI from a non-attached process and matches known copy sizes within 0.005% on DGX Spark, with an MIT-licensed tool, giving Spark owners real memory-bandwidth telemetry for inference tuning.

items.title: Pruna launches P-Video-2-Pro-Lipsync on MiniMax H3: re-sync a talking video to new audio at $0.025 per second
items.summary: An API model that takes an existing talking video plus new audio and re-renders only the mouth, keeping shot, framing and identity, for dubbing and line fixes. Partners list clips up to 60 s at 1080p, about 14 s to process a 5 s clip and 10 tested languages; it is live on Pruna, Runware and each::labs on day one.

doubt.pushback: Vendor and reseller posts only; no independent quality comparison yet.

items.title: Retro Diffusion's RD Flow 64, a 271M-parameter pixel-art text-to-image model, now runs in real time in the browser on WebGPU
items.summary: RD Flow 64 is a small flow-matching model that draws 64x64 pixel-art sprites and game assets, about 74x smaller than Qwen Image 2.1. An ONNX port and static WebGPU Space make it run locally in a browser tab with no server GPU.

items.title: FLUX 3 Action ranks first among VLA and world-action models on Poke & Wiggle's physical Reality Check robot benchmark
items.summary: Poke & Wiggle built an open benchmark that runs robot policies on its own physical stations, and Black Forest Labs reports FLUX 3 Action is the top VLA/WAM there, with every clip under the model's control. This is a second third-party robotics result for the model after RoboColosseum.

doubt.pushback: Vendor-reported rank; leaderboard link not given in the post.

items.title: PyTorch Lightning can checkpoint straight to Hugging Face Storage Buckets and resume from them
items.summary: Pointing Lightning's ModelCheckpoint at an hf://buckets/ path writes checkpoints to a Hugging Face Storage Bucket and resumes training from it, removing the separate upload step for long or preemptible training jobs.

doubt.pushback: No docs or release link in the post.
